Gompertz Analyis of Lifespan in the BXDs by Diet

No QTL yet; just a big picture view

Author

Beni Mozhui

Date

November 20, 2026

Quick Introduction

The Gompertz model says that the risk of dying rises exponentially with age. It is expressed as:

mortality rate at age t = a * exp(b * t)

a = initial mortality rate (the baseline level of risk or the intercept)

b = rate of aging (the slope)

log(2) / b = mortality rate doubling time (MRDT)

For the BXDs, I don’t think adding a Makeham parameter is meaningful. Gompertz-Makeham is an extension of the original Gompertz equation. The Makeham paramerter (g) adds a constant age-independent risk of death due to external causes. In humans, this can vary a lot by country, neighborhood, etc. For example, in some parts of the world, the risk of death due to violence or preventable infectious diseases can be high. In lab mice, young deaths such as due to cage flooding (“unnatural deaths”) are removed.

Part A: CD-HF COMPARISON

Load packages, data, and specify settings

Code 
library(survival)   # survival curves and data splitting
library(flexsurv)   # fits the Gompertz model
library(ggplot2)    # graphs
library(knitr)      # cleaner looking output using kable()
library(MASS)       # for mvrnorm(): random draws from a multivariate normal
Code 
diets_to_compare   <- c("CD", "HF")           

n_boot <- 200                 # bootstrap repeats for confidence intervals
                              # (200 is quick; use 1000 for a final analysis)

set.seed(2026)                # makes the bootstrap give the same result each run

diet_colours <- c(CD = "#494e84", HF = "#dd164c", NAM = "#da9100")

Create a working data frame that has data on strain ID, diet, age at entry, and age at death

Code 
raw <- read.csv("BXD_Lifespan_AllDiets_Dataset_Mapping_Arends.csv",
                skip = 15, check.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
#first 15 lines are metadata notes

mice <- data.frame(
  Diet      = raw$Diet,
  Strain    = raw$Strain,
  Vivarium  = raw$Vivarium,
  age_entry = raw$`Age at set up (days)`,   # age when the mouse entered the study
  age_death = raw$`Age at death (days)`,    # age when the mouse died
  event     = 1                             # 1 = died (every mouse here died)
)

cat("Max age when mice were entered into study =", max(raw$`Age at set up (days)`), "\nMin age when mice were entered into study =", min(raw$`Age at set up (days)`))
Max age when mice were entered into study = 877 
Min age when mice were entered into study = 26

Why are we including age at set up as a variable?

Mice joined the study at different ages. This introduces some biases. For instance, if a mouse joint the study at age 300, that mouse was already preselect to have not died before that entry age. Risk of dying only counts after entry age.

For this reason, we apply a left truncation in the survival analysis.

The survival model will have: Surv(age of entry, age of death, event), where event is either death or censored.

Note: In this case, the only event that matters in death (all mice in this data accepted the finitude of life, and faced their own mortality with grace and courage. We are thankful for their contribution to science).

Fitting Gompertz model to each diet separately

Code 
params <- data.frame()       # empty table; one row per diet is added below

for (diet in diets_to_compare) {

  mice_this_diet <- subset(mice, Diet == diet)

  fit <- flexsurvreg(Surv(age_entry, age_death, event) ~ 1,
                     data = mice_this_diet, dist = "gompertz") #loop to fit for each diet#

  a    <- fit$res["rate",  "est"]
  a_lo <- fit$res["rate",  "L95%"]
  a_hi <- fit$res["rate",  "U95%"]
  b    <- fit$res["shape", "est"]
  b_lo <- fit$res["shape", "L95%"]
  b_hi <- fit$res["shape", "U95%"]

  # Median lifespan predicted by the Gompertz curve
  median_lifespan <- log(1 + b * log(2) / a) / b

  params <- rbind(params, data.frame(
    Diet = diet, n = nrow(mice_this_diet),
    a = a, a_lo = a_lo, a_hi = a_hi,
    b = b, b_lo = b_lo, b_hi = b_hi,
    MRDT = log(2) / b, MRDT_lo = log(2) / b_hi, MRDT_hi = log(2) / b_lo,
    median_lifespan = median_lifespan))
}
# write.csv(params, file="UnadjustedGompertzParamters.csv")
params$Diet <- factor(params$Diet, levels = diets_to_compare)
kable(params, digits = 4)

Strain adjusted analysis

Code 
strain_fit_diet_b <- flexsurvreg(Surv(age_entry, age_death, event) ~ Diet + Strain,
                                anc = list(shape = ~ Diet),
                                data = mice, dist = "gompertz")
                                #main effects of Diet and Strain on intercept a + effect of Diet on slope#
strain_fit_same_b <- flexsurvreg(Surv(age_entry, age_death, event) ~ Diet + Strain,
                                 data = mice, dist = "gompertz")
                                 #only main effect of Diet and Strain on intercept a#
# Note: unlike glm(), calling summary() for a flexsurreg() object will calculate 
# predicted survival metrics (such as survival probabilities, hazard rates, or median survival) over time

# to view model coefficients, simply type object name:
# strain_fit_diet_b
# strain_fit_same_b
# but the output will list individual strains and it will be long and difficult to read

# The diet rows of the results:
#   shape          = b on the reference diet
#   shape(DietHF)  = how much HF ADDS to b
#   DietHF         = how much HF shifts log(a)  (0 = no change in baseline)
#   rate           = a for the reference diet in the reference strain
res <- strain_fit_diet_b$res
kable(res[!grepl("^Strain", rownames(res)), ])

# Does diet change b within strains?  (likelihood-ratio test, as in STEP 6)
LR_b_strain <- 2 * (strain_fit_diet_b$loglik - strain_fit_same_b$loglik) #the only difference
# between _own_ and _same_ is the anc=list(shapr= ~ Diet) term, and this computes the 
# effect of that term on the model

cat("Within strains, does diet change b?  LR =", round(LR_b_strain, 2),
    " p =", signif(pchisq(LR_b_strain, length(diets_to_compare) - 1,
                          lower.tail = FALSE), 3), "\n")
Within strains, does diet change b?  LR = 12.91  p = 0.000326
Code 
## a and b for a "typical" strain on each diet --------------------------------
# a depends on the strain, so we report it for a typical strain: the average
# of all strain effects on the log(a) scale. The reference strain's effect
# is 0 (it has no row of its own).

# coef() returns a numeric vector of the model's maximum likelihood parameter estimates

all_coefs     <- coef(strain_fit_diet_b)        # this extracts the estimates from the statistical resuls  
                                                                # everything on the log scale (ln)
                                                # (except shape, which is not logged)
strain_names  <- levels(factor(mice$Strain))    # the first one is the reference
strain_effect <- c(0, all_coefs[grepl("^Strain", names(all_coefs))])
names(strain_effect)[1] <- paste0("Strain", strain_names[1])
typical_strain_effect <- mean(strain_effect)

adjusted_params <- data.frame()
for (diet in diets_to_compare) {
  log_a <- all_coefs["rate"] + typical_strain_effect
  b     <- all_coefs["shape"]
  if (diet != diets_to_compare[1]) {             # add the diet shifts
                                                 # alternatively for CD vs HF, if(diet == "HF")         
    log_a <- log_a + all_coefs[paste0("Diet", diet)]
    b     <- b     + all_coefs[paste0("shape(Diet", diet, ")")]
  }
  adjusted_params <- rbind(adjusted_params, data.frame(
    Diet = diet, a = exp(log_a), b = b, MRDT = log(2) / b,
    median_lifespan = log(1 + b * log(2) / exp(log_a)) / b))
}
adjusted_params$Diet <- factor(adjusted_params$Diet, levels = diets_to_compare)
kable(adjusted_params, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
The Gompertz parameters after adjusting for strain
Diet a b MRDT median_lifespan
CD 1e-04 0.0058 119.5052 632.4095
HF 1e-04 0.0067 104.0197 564.2062

Why is it important to adjust for strain?

Because the BXDs are a heterogeneous population and some strains die early. Many of the early mortality may be due to age-independent causes. If we do not adjusted for Strain, HF will have an effect, but it will be difficult to clarify if HF reduces a (the intercept) or b (the slope). Not controlling for strain differences at intercept will underestimate b and it will be difficult to discern the differences in slope.

In the above equation: “~ Diet + Strain”: each strain has its own a, and this adjusts for baseline differences between strains, and estimates how diet shifts a after adjusting for strain difference

By adding the ancillary “anc = list(shape = ~ Diet)”, it determines the b(rate) for each diet has its own b (rate) after adjusting for baseline differences between strains.

Code 
strain_weight <- data.frame(
  Strain = strain_names,
  Effect = strain_effect,
  weight = exp(strain_effect[paste0("Strain", strain_names)] - typical_strain_effect),
  row.names = NULL)

# can safe individual strain weight
# write.csv(strain_weight, file="strain_weigths.csv")


bins_adj <- survSplit(Surv(age_entry, age_death, event) ~ Diet + Strain,
                      data = mice, cut = seq(0, 1400, by = 50)) #this splits the data into 50 day bins#
                      # converts "one-row-per-mouse" into a "one-row-per-time-interval" format
                      # A mouse that lives to day 900 produces 18 rows (900 / 50) instead of just 1
                      
bins_adj$days_at_risk <- bins_adj$age_death - bins_adj$age_entry
bins_adj$age_bin      <- floor(bins_adj$age_entry / 50) * 50 + 25
bins_adj$weight       <- strain_weight$weight[match(bins_adj$Strain, strain_weight$Strain)]
bins_adj$weighted_days <- bins_adj$days_at_risk * bins_adj$weight

observed_adj <- aggregate(cbind(event, weighted_days) ~ Diet + age_bin,
                          data = bins_adj, FUN = sum)
observed_adj$mortality <- observed_adj$event / observed_adj$weighted_days
observed_adj <- subset(observed_adj, event >= 3)

adjusted_lines <- data.frame()
ages <- seq(100, 1200, by = 10)
for (i in 1:nrow(adjusted_params)) {
  adjusted_lines <- rbind(adjusted_lines, data.frame(
    age = ages, Diet = adjusted_params$Diet[i],
    mortality = adjusted_params$a[i] * exp(adjusted_params$b[i] * ages)))
}

plot_mortality_adjusted <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = observed_adj, aes(age_bin, mortality, colour = Diet,
                                      size = event), alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_line(data = adjusted_lines, aes(age, mortality, colour = Diet),
            linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = diet_colours) +
  labs(title = "Strain-adjusted mortality rate by age (log scale)", #subtitles can be added with subtitle = "text here"
       x = "Age (days)", y = "Deaths per mouse per day", size = "Deaths") +
  annotate(geom = "text",
    x = Inf, y = 0,                # x = -Inf, y = -Inf for bottom-left corner of the plot panel
                                       # this moves the achor points to the far corners of plots
                                      # as it's on log scale, y = -Inf should be y = 0
    label = "CD: a=0.0001; b=0.0058; MRDT=120\nHF: a=0.0001; b=0.0066; MRDT=104",
    hjust = 1.1, vjust = -0.5,        # Nudge slightly left and up
                                      # hjust/vjust controls horizontal and vertical alighments
    size = 3.5, color = "darkred") + # to italicize, add fontface = "italic"

How much does diet effect a and/or b?

We can decompose the relative contribution of diet to a and b.

The results indicate the HF mostly shifts the rate of aging (ie., b). This becomes clear after fitting Strain as a cofactor. Exclude strain, and the results will say that HF shifts the intercept, but this may not be accurate.

Code 
## Does diet change a, b, after adjusting for strain differences in intercept? ----

s_model_no_diet <- flexsurvreg(Surv(age_entry, age_death, event) ~ Strain,
                               data = mice, dist = "gompertz")
s_model_a_only  <- flexsurvreg(Surv(age_entry, age_death, event) ~ Diet + Strain,
                               data = mice, dist = "gompertz")
s_model_b_only  <- flexsurvreg(Surv(age_entry, age_death, event) ~ Strain,
                               anc = list(shape = ~ Diet),
                               data = mice, dist = "gompertz")
s_model_both    <- flexsurvreg(Surv(age_entry, age_death, event) ~ Diet + Strain,
                               anc = list(shape = ~ Diet),
                               data = mice, dist = "gompertz")

LR_any_s <- 2 * (s_model_both$loglik - s_model_no_diet$loglik)
LR_a_s   <- 2 * (s_model_both$loglik - s_model_b_only$loglik)
LR_b_s   <- 2 * (s_model_both$loglik - s_model_a_only$loglik)

extra_df <- length(diets_to_compare) - 1
tests_strain <- data.frame(
  question = c("Does diet have any effect? (within strains)",
               "Does diet change a? (within strains)",
               "Does diet change b? (within strains)"),
  LR = c(LR_any_s, LR_a_s, LR_b_s),
  df = c(2 * extra_df, extra_df, extra_df))
tests_strain$p_value <- pchisq(tests_strain$LR, tests_strain$df, lower.tail = FALSE)
print(tests_strain, digits = 3)
                                     question       LR df  p_value

3        Does diet change b? (within strains)  12.9138  1 3.26e-04

# write.csv(tests_strain, file="gompertz_tests_strainadjusted.csv")
Code 
n_draws <- 2000

coef_hat <- coef(s_model_both)
draws <- rbind(coef_hat,                                      # draw 0 = estimate
               mvrnorm(n_draws, mu = coef_hat, Sigma = vcov(s_model_both)))

strain_columns <- grepl("^Strain", colnames(draws))
n_strains      <- sum(strain_columns) + 1             # +1 for the reference strain
diet_pairs <- combn(diets_to_compare, 2)

decomposition_strain <- data.frame()


for (k in 1:ncol(diet_pairs)) {

  ref <- diet_pairs[1, k]
  alt <- diet_pairs[2, k]
  results <- data.frame()

  for (d in 1:nrow(draws)) {
    cf <- draws[d, ]

    # typical strain = average strain effect (reference strain counts as 0)
    typical <- sum(cf[strain_columns]) / n_strains

    # log a and b for each diet; the first diet is the reference (no shift)
    log_a <- c(); b <- c()
    for (diet in c(ref, alt)) {
      la <- cf["rate"] + typical
      bb <- cf["shape"]
      if (diet != diets_to_compare[1]) {
        la <- la + cf[paste0("Diet", diet)]
        bb <- bb + cf[paste0("shape(Diet", diet, ")")]
      }
      log_a <- c(log_a, la); b <- c(b, bb)
    }
    a1 <- exp(log_a[1]); b1 <- b[1]          # reference diet
    a2 <- exp(log_a[2]); b2 <- b[2]          # other diet

    med_a1_b1 <- log(1 + b1 * log(2) / a1) / b1
    med_a2_b2 <- log(1 + b2 * log(2) / a2) / b2
    med_a2_b1 <- log(1 + b1 * log(2) / a2) / b1
    med_a1_b2 <- log(1 + b2 * log(2) / a1) / b2

    results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
      draw     = d - 1,
      total    = med_a2_b2 - med_a1_b1,
      due_to_a = ((med_a2_b1 - med_a1_b1) + (med_a2_b2 - med_a1_b2)) / 2,
      due_to_b = ((med_a1_b2 - med_a1_b1) + (med_a2_b2 - med_a2_b1)) / 2))
  }

  real <- results[results$draw == 0, ]
  sims <- results[results$draw > 0, ]

  decomposition_strain <- rbind(decomposition_strain, data.frame(
    contrast  = paste(alt, "minus", ref),
    component = c("Total change", "Due to a", "Due to b"),
    estimate  = c(real$total, real$due_to_a, real$due_to_b),
    lower_95  = c(quantile(sims$total, 0.025), quantile(sims$due_to_a, 0.025),
                  quantile(sims$due_to_b, 0.025)),
    upper_95  = c(quantile(sims$total, 0.975), quantile(sims$due_to_a, 0.975),
                  quantile(sims$due_to_b, 0.975))))
}

kable(decomposition_strain, digits = 3)

Survival plots

We plot the observed survival curve, and compare it to the predicted survival curve based on the Gompertz functions. Here we compare between the observed data vs the strain adjusted Gompertz fit and the strain unadjusted Gompertz fit.

Strain-dependent frailty results in early death and without the strain correction, there are more predicted deaths for the HF mice before 500 days based on the estimated Gompertz a and b.

Code 
start_age <- 100
mice_100  <- subset(mice, age_death > start_age)
mice_100$age_entry <- pmax(mice_100$age_entry, start_age)

km <- survfit(Surv(age_entry, age_death, event) ~ Diet, data = mice_100)
km_table <- data.frame(age      = km$time,
                       survival = km$surv,
                       Diet     = rep(diets_to_compare, km$strata))

# Gompertz survival: S(t) = exp(-(a/b) * (exp(b*t) - 1)),
# divided by S(100) so it also starts at 100 days
ages <- seq(start_age, 1300, by = 5)

fit_curves <- data.frame()
for (i in 1:nrow(params)) {
  a <- params$a[i]; b <- params$b[i]
  S_t   <- exp(-(a / b) * (exp(b * ages) - 1))
  S_100 <- exp(-(a / b) * (exp(b * start_age) - 1))
  fit_curves <- rbind(fit_curves,
                      data.frame(age = ages, survival = S_t / S_100,
                                 Diet = params$Diet[i]))
}


fit_curvesAdj <- data.frame()
ages <- seq(start_age, 1300, by = 5)
for (i in 1:nrow(adjusted_params)) {
  a <- adjusted_params$a[i]; b <- adjusted_params$b[i]
  S_t   <- exp(-(a / b) * (exp(b * ages) - 1))
  S_100 <- exp(-(a / b) * (exp(b * start_age) - 1))
  fit_curvesAdj <- rbind(fit_curvesAdj,
                      data.frame(age = ages, survival = S_t / S_100,
                                 Diet = adjusted_params$Diet[i]))
}


plot_survival <- ggplot() +
  geom_step(data = km_table,   aes(age, survival, colour = Diet)) +
  geom_line(data = fit_curves, aes(age, survival, colour = Diet),
            linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_line(data = fit_curvesAdj, aes(age, survival, colour = Diet),
            linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = diet_colours) +
  labs(title = "Survival: observed (solid) vs unadjusted Gompertz (dotted)\nvs strain adjusted Gompertz (dashed)",
       x = "Age (days)", y = "Proportion alive (given alive at 100 days)") +  
  theme_bw()
plot_survival

Part C: CD-HF-NAM COMPARISON

Load packages, data and specify settings

Cleared the previous session for a fresh start.

So re-load the packages and data

Code 
library(survival)   # survival curves and data splitting
library(flexsurv)   # fits the Gompertz model
library(ggplot2)    # graphs
library(knitr)      # cleaner looking output using kable()
library(MASS)       # for mvrnorm(): random draws from a multivariate normal
Code 
diets_to_compare   <- c("CD", "HF", "NAM")           

n_boot <- 200                 # bootstrap repeats for confidence intervals
                              # (200 is quick; use 1000 for a final analysis)

set.seed(2026)                # makes the bootstrap give the same result each run

diet_colours <- c(CD = "#494e84", HF = "#dd164c", NAM = "#da9100")

Create a working data frame that has data on strain ID, diet, age at entry, and age at death.

Code 
raw <- read.csv("BXD_Lifespan_AllDiets_Dataset_Mapping_Arends.csv",
                skip = 15, check.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
#first 15 lines are metadata notes

mice <- data.frame(
  Diet      = raw$Diet,
  Strain    = raw$Strain,
  Vivarium  = raw$Vivarium,
  age_entry = raw$`Age at set up (days)`,   # age when the mouse entered the study
  age_death = raw$`Age at death (days)`,    # age when the mouse died
  event     = 1                             # 1 = died (every mouse here died)
)

Select the mice

In this part, we want the CD, HF and NAM mice. We also want to keep only the strains that have NAM data so that no biases are introduced.

Code 
# Keep only the diets chosen in STEP 0
mice <- subset(mice, Diet %in% diets_to_compare)
nam_strains <- unique(raw$Strain[raw$Diet == "NAM"])
mice <- subset(mice, Strain %in% nam_strains)

# Make Diet a factor with the first diet listed as the reference group
mice$Diet <- factor(mice$Diet, levels = diets_to_compare)

Fitting Gompertz model to each diet separately

Code 
params <- data.frame()       # empty table; one row per diet is added below

for (diet in diets_to_compare) {

  mice_this_diet <- subset(mice, Diet == diet)

  fit <- flexsurvreg(Surv(age_entry, age_death, event) ~ 1,
                     data = mice_this_diet, dist = "gompertz") #loop to fit for each diet#

  a    <- fit$res["rate",  "est"]
  a_lo <- fit$res["rate",  "L95%"]
  a_hi <- fit$res["rate",  "U95%"]
  b    <- fit$res["shape", "est"]
  b_lo <- fit$res["shape", "L95%"]
  b_hi <- fit$res["shape", "U95%"]

  # Median lifespan predicted by the Gompertz curve
  median_lifespan <- log(1 + b * log(2) / a) / b

  params <- rbind(params, data.frame(
    Diet = diet, n = nrow(mice_this_diet),
    a = a, a_lo = a_lo, a_hi = a_hi,
    b = b, b_lo = b_lo, b_hi = b_hi,
    MRDT = log(2) / b, MRDT_lo = log(2) / b_hi, MRDT_hi = log(2) / b_lo,
    median_lifespan = median_lifespan))
}
# write.csv(params, file="NAM.UnadjustedGompertzParamters.csv")
params$Diet <- factor(params$Diet, levels = diets_to_compare)
kable(params, digits = 4)

# Does diet change b within strains?  (likelihood-ratio test, as in STEP 6)
LR_b_strain <- 2 * (strain_fit_diet_b$loglik - strain_fit_same_b$loglik) #the only difference
# between _own_ and _same_ is the anc=list(shapr= ~ Diet) term, and this computes the 
# effect of that term on the model

Code 
## a and b for a "typical" strain on each diet --------------------------------
# a depends on the strain, so we report it for a typical strain: the average
# of all strain effects on the log(a) scale. The reference strain's effect
# is 0 (it has no row of its own).

# coef() returns a numeric vector of the model's maximum likelihood parameter estimates

all_coefs     <- coef(strain_fit_diet_b)        # this extracts the estimates from the statistical resuls  
                                                                # everything on the log scale (ln)
                                                # (except shape, which is not logged)
strain_names  <- levels(factor(mice$Strain))    # the first one is the reference
strain_effect <- c(0, all_coefs[grepl("^Strain", names(all_coefs))])
names(strain_effect)[1] <- paste0("Strain", strain_names[1])
typical_strain_effect <- mean(strain_effect)

adjusted_params <- data.frame()
for (diet in diets_to_compare) {
  log_a <- all_coefs["rate"] + typical_strain_effect
  b     <- all_coefs["shape"]
  if (diet != diets_to_compare[1]) {             # add the diet shifts
                                                 # alternatively for CD vs HF, if(diet == "HF")         
    log_a <- log_a + all_coefs[paste0("Diet", diet)]
    b     <- b     + all_coefs[paste0("shape(Diet", diet, ")")]
  }
  adjusted_params <- rbind(adjusted_params, data.frame(
    Diet = diet, a = exp(log_a), b = b, MRDT = log(2) / b,
    median_lifespan = log(1 + b * log(2) / exp(log_a)) / b))
}
adjusted_params$Diet <- factor(adjusted_params$Diet, levels = diets_to_compare)
kable(adjusted_params, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)

bins_adj <- survSplit(Surv(age_entry, age_death, event) ~ Diet + Strain,
                      data = mice, cut = seq(0, 1400, by = 50)) #this splits the data into 50 day bins#
                      # converts "one-row-per-mouse" into a "one-row-per-time-interval" format
                      # A mouse that lives to day 900 produces 18 rows (900 / 50) instead of just 1
                      
bins_adj$days_at_risk <- bins_adj$age_death - bins_adj$age_entry
bins_adj$age_bin      <- floor(bins_adj$age_entry / 50) * 50 + 25
bins_adj$weight       <- strain_weight$weight[match(bins_adj$Strain, strain_weight$Strain)]
bins_adj$weighted_days <- bins_adj$days_at_risk * bins_adj$weight

observed_adj <- aggregate(cbind(event, weighted_days) ~ Diet + age_bin,
                          data = bins_adj, FUN = sum)
observed_adj$mortality <- observed_adj$event / observed_adj$weighted_days
observed_adj <- subset(observed_adj, event >= 3)

    mortality = adjusted_params$a[i] * exp(adjusted_params$b[i] * ages)))

## Does diet change a, b, after adjusting for strain differences in intercept? ----

s_model_no_diet <- flexsurvreg(Surv(age_entry, age_death, event) ~ Strain,
                               data = mice, dist = "gompertz")
s_model_a_only  <- flexsurvreg(Surv(age_entry, age_death, event) ~ Diet + Strain,
                               data = mice, dist = "gompertz")
s_model_b_only  <- flexsurvreg(Surv(age_entry, age_death, event) ~ Strain,
                               anc = list(shape = ~ Diet),
                               data = mice, dist = "gompertz")
s_model_both    <- flexsurvreg(Surv(age_entry, age_death, event) ~ Diet + Strain,
                               anc = list(shape = ~ Diet),
                               data = mice, dist = "gompertz")

LR_any_s <- 2 * (s_model_both$loglik - s_model_no_diet$loglik)
LR_a_s   <- 2 * (s_model_both$loglik - s_model_b_only$loglik)
LR_b_s   <- 2 * (s_model_both$loglik - s_model_a_only$loglik)

extra_df <- length(diets_to_compare) - 1
tests_strain <- data.frame(
  question = c("Does diet have any effect? (within strains)",
               "Does diet change a? (within strains)",
               "Does diet change b? (within strains)"),
  LR = c(LR_any_s, LR_a_s, LR_b_s),
  df = c(2 * extra_df, extra_df, extra_df))
tests_strain$p_value <- pchisq(tests_strain$LR, tests_strain$df, lower.tail = FALSE)

Code 
n_draws <- 2000

coef_hat <- coef(s_model_both)
draws <- rbind(coef_hat,                                      # draw 0 = estimate
               mvrnorm(n_draws, mu = coef_hat, Sigma = vcov(s_model_both)))

strain_columns <- grepl("^Strain", colnames(draws))
n_strains      <- sum(strain_columns) + 1             # +1 for the reference strain
diet_pairs <- combn(diets_to_compare, 2)

decomposition_strain <- data.frame()


for (k in 1:ncol(diet_pairs)) {

  ref <- diet_pairs[1, k]
  alt <- diet_pairs[2, k]
  results <- data.frame()

  for (d in 1:nrow(draws)) {
    cf <- draws[d, ]

    # typical strain = average strain effect (reference strain counts as 0)
    typical <- sum(cf[strain_columns]) / n_strains

    # log a and b for each diet; the first diet is the reference (no shift)
    log_a <- c(); b <- c()
    for (diet in c(ref, alt)) {
      la <- cf["rate"] + typical
      bb <- cf["shape"]
      if (diet != diets_to_compare[1]) {
        la <- la + cf[paste0("Diet", diet)]
        bb <- bb + cf[paste0("shape(Diet", diet, ")")]
      }
      log_a <- c(log_a, la); b <- c(b, bb)
    }
    a1 <- exp(log_a[1]); b1 <- b[1]          # reference diet
    a2 <- exp(log_a[2]); b2 <- b[2]          # other diet

    med_a1_b1 <- log(1 + b1 * log(2) / a1) / b1
    med_a2_b2 <- log(1 + b2 * log(2) / a2) / b2
    med_a2_b1 <- log(1 + b1 * log(2) / a2) / b1
    med_a1_b2 <- log(1 + b2 * log(2) / a1) / b2

    results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
      draw     = d - 1,
      total    = med_a2_b2 - med_a1_b1,
      due_to_a = ((med_a2_b1 - med_a1_b1) + (med_a2_b2 - med_a1_b2)) / 2,
      due_to_b = ((med_a1_b2 - med_a1_b1) + (med_a2_b2 - med_a2_b1)) / 2))
  }

  real <- results[results$draw == 0, ]
  sims <- results[results$draw > 0, ]

  decomposition_strain <- rbind(decomposition_strain, data.frame(
    contrast  = paste(alt, "minus", ref),
    component = c("Total change", "Due to a", "Due to b"),
    estimate  = c(real$total, real$due_to_a, real$due_to_b),
    lower_95  = c(quantile(sims$total, 0.025), quantile(sims$due_to_a, 0.025),
                  quantile(sims$due_to_b, 0.025)),
    upper_95  = c(quantile(sims$total, 0.975), quantile(sims$due_to_a, 0.975),
                  quantile(sims$due_to_b, 0.975))))
}

Survival plots

We plot the observed survival curve, and plot the predicted survival curve based on the Gompertz functions. Here we only compare betweenthe observed data vs the strain adjusted Gompertz fit.

Code 
start_age <- 100
mice_100  <- subset(mice, age_death > start_age)
mice_100$age_entry <- pmax(mice_100$age_entry, start_age)

km <- survfit(Surv(age_entry, age_death, event) ~ Diet, data = mice_100)
km_table <- data.frame(age      = km$time,
                       survival = km$surv,
                       Diet     = rep(diets_to_compare, km$strata))

# Gompertz survival: S(t) = exp(-(a/b) * (exp(b*t) - 1)),
# divided by S(100) so it also starts at 100 days
ages <- seq(start_age, 1300, by = 5)

fit_curves <- data.frame()
for (i in 1:nrow(params)) {
  a <- params$a[i]; b <- params$b[i]
  S_t   <- exp(-(a / b) * (exp(b * ages) - 1))
  S_100 <- exp(-(a / b) * (exp(b * start_age) - 1))
  fit_curves <- rbind(fit_curves,
                      data.frame(age = ages, survival = S_t / S_100,
                                 Diet = params$Diet[i]))
}


fit_curvesAdj <- data.frame()
ages <- seq(start_age, 1300, by = 5)
for (i in 1:nrow(adjusted_params)) {
  a <- adjusted_params$a[i]; b <- adjusted_params$b[i]
  S_t   <- exp(-(a / b) * (exp(b * ages) - 1))
  S_100 <- exp(-(a / b) * (exp(b * start_age) - 1))
  fit_curvesAdj <- rbind(fit_curvesAdj,
                      data.frame(age = ages, survival = S_t / S_100,
                                 Diet = adjusted_params$Diet[i]))
}


plot_survival <- ggplot() +
  geom_step(data = km_table,   aes(age, survival, colour = Diet)) +
  geom_line(data = fit_curvesAdj, aes(age, survival, colour = Diet),
            linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = diet_colours) +
  labs(title = "Survival: observed (solid) vs strain adjusted Gompertz (dashed)",
       x = "Age (days)", y = "Proportion alive (given alive at 100 days)") +  
  theme_bw()
plot_survival
